transcript.text: Just got a new Siemens dishwasher and there's always a bit of water left in the bottom under the filter after it finishes. Is it draining properly?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Probably, yes. A small amount of clean water left in the sump under the filter is normal on most dishwashers, Siemens included. The pump can't get every last drop out of the sump, and a little water left there keeps the pump seals from drying out. A cupful or so sitting below the filter level is exactly what you'd expect. It would point to a drainage problem instead if:
• the water sits above the filter or covers the base of the tub
• it's dirty, greasy or has bits of food in it
• it smells
• the amount keeps growing or the machine stops mid-cycle with an error If you want to be sure, these quick checks tell normal apart from a part-blockage: 1. Look at the level after a cycle. Clean water just in the sump below the filter is normal and you can leave it. Water up over the filter means it isn't pumping out fully, so go on to the next checks.
2. Take out the lower rack, twist and lift out the filter, and rinse it under the tap. If it's clogged with food or grease, cleaning it may be all it needs. On a new machine it should be fairly clean. Get into the habit of rinsing it every couple of weeks.
3. Because it's a new install, check the grey drain hose behind the plinth and under the sink isn't kinked or squashed. Also check where it joins the sink waste: on a newly fitted spigot there's a blanking plug inside that has to be cut out. If the hose is kinked or the plug is still in, the machine will struggle to drain and you'd usually see more water than a cupful. If the water stays clean and below the filter, there's nothing to fix. If it's above the filter or dirty even after those checks, let me know and we'll look at the pump side. Roughly how much water is there, and is it clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]

Thanks, that's reassuring. It's roughly a cupful, just covering the bottom of the sump under the filter, and none in the main tub. The water looks clean. The filter is clean too and the drain hose is looped up under the sink with no kinks.

That's all normal, and you can stop worrying about it. A cupful of clean water sitting in the sump under the filter, with the main tub dry, is what a dishwasher that is draining properly looks like. The pump can't get the last bit out of the sump, and that water keeps the pump seals from drying out between washes. You've already ruled out the usual culprits: the filter is clean and the hose is looped up with no kinks. Having the hose looped up under the sink is right, by the way, because the high loop stops dirty sink water running back into the machine. There's nothing to fix. 1. The water rises above the filter or spreads across the floor of the tub. That would point to a partial blockage, usually at the sink waste or trap, or something caught at the pump.
2. Clean the filter first; if that doesn't sort it, there's probably a restriction on the drain side.
3. The machine stops mid-cycle with an error or beeps, which is usually a drain fault. If any of those turns up, come back and we'll work through the pump side. Otherwise, rinse the filter every couple of weeks and enjoy the new machine.

candidates: Normal residual water in the sump (keeps seals wet) (high)
Partially blocked drain filter or sump (low)
Drain hose kinked or sink-waste blanking plug left in after a new install (low)
